interface.signature: def getHappyString(n: int, k: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: The length n is between 1 and 10 inclusive.
The index k is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '' or (len(return_value) == n and all(return_value[i] in 'abc' for i in range(n)) and all(return_value[i] != return_value[i+1] for i in range(n-1)))
postconditions.description: If the result is non-empty, it must be a happy string of length n (only 'a','b','c' and no adjacent identical characters).

postconditions.expression: return_value == '' or (return_value == sorted_happy_strings[n-1][k-1] if k <= len(sorted_happy_strings[n-1]) else False)
postconditions.description: If k is within the count of happy strings of length n, return_value is the k-th string in lexicographical order; otherwise it is empty. Here sorted_happy_strings[n-1] denotes the list of all happy strings of length n sorted lexicographically.
The total number of happy strings of length n is 3 * 2^(n-1); if k exceeds this count, the result is an empty string.
